items.title: The Yen Is Becoming Too Hard for Some Investors to Trade
points: (Bloomberg) -- After a year of wild swings, the yen surprised traders by settling into a tight range clustered near 158 per dollar over recent months.
But on Wednesday it broke out again, unexpectedly weakening toward 160.
The yen is one of the world’s most heavily traded currencies, changing hands in some $1.6 trillion of transactions each day.

“The challenge is that these competing forces have made the timing and magnitude of yen moves much harder to anticipate,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA, which manages about 600 million Swiss francs in assets.
Japan has spent a record ¥27.1 trillion ($169.7 billion) buying yen this year, almost three times the nation’s combined trade deficit and direct-investment outflows.
But decades of cheap money have left Japan with ¥811 trillion in overseas portfolio assets and patterns of overseas investment that may prove difficult to reverse.

items.title: Anthropic’s IPO Is About Six Times Oversubscribed
points: (Bloomberg) -- Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering has drawn about six times the orders for the shares available, according to people familiar with the matter, as interest increases for potentially the biggest first-time share sale ever.
The Claude AI model firm and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in the IPO and $26 billion in a private placement, its filings show.
The chipmaker has agreed to buy about $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic as part of a $26 billion private placement concurrent with its IPO, the AI model firm’s filings show.
The company is targeting a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion, below where some investors expected the company to settle, Bloomberg News reported.
The company reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of Oct.
31, up $10 billion from the end of September, the filing showed.
Anthropic had a $65 billion run rate figure at the end of July, Bloomberg News reported.

items.title: Rockstar Joins Chinese TikTok Platform Douyin to Promote GTA 6 in China
points: Rockstar Games is expanding its GTA 6 marketing campaign in China.
The company has reportedly joined Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok, ahead of the game’s November 19, 2026 release.
Its first video promotes the game’s upcoming launch and pre-loading availability on both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
According to a November 12 report by GamerSky, Rockstar’s Douyin account is officially verified under the name “ROCKSTAR INTERNATIONAL LIMITED,” with its IP location listed as Shanghai, China.
The video has been adapted into a vertical format to suit Douyin’s short-video platform and features GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia.
The download requires up to 212 GB of available storage, depending on the console.
The company previously joined Bilibili in 2023, where it has promoted games from the Grand Theft Auto Online and Red Dead Redemption franchises.
Despite its growing presence on Chinese social media, Rockstar has not announced an official mainland China release for GTA 6.

Trafigura, one of the largest aluminum traders, has built up a significant long position in the LME aluminum market as it seeks metal that could be sold at a profit in China, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified…
LME data show several large holders of long positions in short-dated aluminum contracts ahead of the expiry next Wednesday of the main contract for November.
The positions in the November contract identified in the LME’s data are collectively larger than the entire 226,350 tons of exchange stocks, which are at the lowest since 1990.

“The LME also routinely requests further position management information from market participants and has the power to require positions to be managed as appropriate.” Trafigura’s move comes as the Chinese aluminum market is undergoing a major squeeze of…

items.title: Fortnite Leak Reveals Scott Pilgrim Collab Coming Soon
points: Fortnite Treasure Hunters Mini Season is already crammed with collabs, and based on recent leaks, there might be one more coming our way.
According to a new leak, which was uncovered during the downtime for Fortnite update 43.10, a collab with Scott Pilgrim is reportedly coming soon.
On November 12, 2026, veteran leaker HYPEX posted on X, sharing details about an encrypted file that was found during the recent Fortnite downtime.
While there’s nothing unusual about the file, the cosmetics within share similarities with Scott Pilgrim; not the film, but the Netflix adaptation called Scott Pilgrim Takes Off.
Based on these findings, this is no doubt related to a Scott Pilgrim collab in Fortnite Treasure Hunters, which could arrive next week.
By the looks of things, the collab with Scott Pilgrim in Fortnite Treasure Hunters will not be limited to just skins, and just well, as the community is really excited.

items.title: US stocks: Retail buyers limit Nvidia stock rout
points: Retail investors poured a record $111 million into Nvidia shares during Thursday’s first half-hour of trading, helping the stock trim an opening loss of as much as 14% to about 5%.
The dip-buying suggests confidence in the AI trade remains resilient despite CEO Jensen Huang’s departure and Nvidia’s loss of more than $1 trillion in market value over five weeks.

items.title: Five held for kidnapping, assaulting youth in Keralam’s Tirur
points: Five people, including three women, were arrested for allegedly kidnapping and assaulting a youth from Pattambi after plotting to end his relationship with one of the women.
The arrested were Safana, 19, from Pattambi, Nadia, 20, and Rabeeba, 25, both from Annara, Tirur, and their male friends Irshad, 28, and Azharudheen, 25, both from Paravanna.
The police arrested them from Thazhepalam, Tirur.

The police said Irshad and Azharudheen had faced action under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) and were involved in several criminal cases, including drug trafficking, attempted murder and assault.
The five were produced before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court at Tirur and remanded in judicial custody.

items.title: Three of Malappuram family killed in Fujairah road crash
points: Three members of a family from Kunnumpuram near Kondotty in Malappuram district, including a three-year-old child, were killed in a road crash in Fujairah, UAE, on Wednesday night.
The deceased were identified as Mohammed Asmil, 21, his twin sister Misna Jubin, 21, and her three-year-old son Mohammed Faiz.
The accident occurred on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Street near the entrance to the Emirate of Fujairah.
According to preliminary reports, a truck that went out of control rammed several vehicles, triggering a massive pile-up.
A few others were also reported to have been killed in the accident.

items.title: US Fed sets new meeting schedule for 2027, as foretold by Chairman Kevin Warsh
points: The Federal Reserve will hold seven rate-setting meetings in 2027 instead of the customary eight, while dedicating its October gathering to broader monetary-policy strategy.
The revised schedule also moves the year’s final policy meeting to November and removes designations for quarterly economic projections as Chair Kevin Warsh reviews the Fed’s communication practices.

items.title: New report identifies Hong Kong’s place in world shipping
points: Hong Kong Maritime Week is about to kick off.
To celebrate the occasion, Splash today publishes a 48-page magazine on the city’s maritime hub credentials.
A ship can be ordered at a mainland Chinese yard, owned through a leasing company in Hong Kong, insured in London, crewed through a management operation in Asia and chartered from Singapore.
Its cargo need never pass through Hong Kong’s harbour.
Hong Kong remains fourth in the 2026 Xinhua-Baltic international maritime centre rankings, behind Singapore, Shanghai and London.
Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou have grown into maritime giants whose physical advantages Hong Kong cannot realistically overturn.

Together they define the central question running through this special report: whether Hong Kong can convert its inherited maritime strengths into a sustainable business model for 2030, even as its traditional measures of importance become less flattering.
Richard Hext, chairman of the Hong Kong Shipowners Association, resists the suggestion that the city is being reduced to an adjunct of the mainland.

items.title: Port of Los Angeles Sets October Cargo Record as Strike Threat and Rail Delays Loom
points: The Port of Los Angeles handled a record 1,026,872 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) in October, marking its second-busiest month ever and extending the strongest five-month cargo run in the port’s 118-year history.
The October total followed September’s all-time record of 1,042,652 TEUs, marking the first time the nation’s busiest container port has surpassed 1 million units in consecutive months.
Loaded imports reached 538,620 TEUs in October, up 25% from a year earlier and 30% above the port’s five-year October average.
Loaded exports totaled 114,981 TEUs, down 7% from October 2025.
Through October, Los Angeles has handled 9,108,497 TEUs, 5% ahead of last year and 9% above its five-year average.

The Pacific Maritime Association and International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26, which represents about 250 maritime watchmen at the ports, have extended contract negotiations through November 20.
Recent port data showed approximately 9,500 rail-bound import containers at Los Angeles had been waiting nine days or longer for on-dock rail transportation.

The court also ordered a compensation of ₹5 lakh for the survivor from the victim compensation fund.

items.title: Eye donation awareness programme organised at Ernakulam MCH
points: The Government Medical College Hospital (MCH), Ernakulam, and the Kerala State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (K-SOTTO) jointly organised an eye donation awareness programme at the hospital on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
The event was held ahead of the hospital’s application for a licence to perform corneal transplantation, according to a communication.
A special internal counselling team was formed as part of the programme to streamline eye donation and corneal transplantation activities at the hospital.
The team will be responsible for communicating with the relatives of deceased patients and explaining the importance of eye donation.
Its members will also receive specialised training in the technical and legal aspects of corneal donation and transplantation.

items.title: Restrictions on me arbitrary, vague: Sonam Wangchuk
points: Invoking Section 163(1) of the BNSS, the Ladakh administration on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) evening shifted Mr. Wangchuk from a protest venue to his residence in Leh and has been allegedly restrained from leaving his residence.
“I was driven towards my village, where my residence is and was eventually taken to HIAL, reaching there at approximately 8.40 p.m. [on Wednesday].
I was told to remain at home under the supervision of police guards.

Since that evening, dozens of armed police personnel [approximately 20 to 22] have been stationed at and around my residence,” said Mr. Wangchuk in a letter to senior officials of Ladakh and the Union Home Ministry.
The order is clearly bad in law, arbitrary, vague and disproportionate.

The Ladakh activist, who was arrested in September last year under the National Security Act (NSA) and released in March this year, said the Ladakh administration’s order “conspicuously does not use words such as “house arrest”.

items.title: Saronic Awards $100 Million-Plus Contract for World’s Largest Shiplift at Texas Shipyard
points: A rendering of Saronic's planned Port Alpha shipyard in Brownsville, Texas.
The company plans to invest more than $3 billion in the next-generation facility, which is expected to begin operations in 2028.

Saronic has awarded a contract worth more than $100 million to Norway’s Syncrolift to design and supply what the companies say will be the world’s largest shiplift at its planned $3 billion Port Alpha shipyard in Brownsville, Texas.

The system will feature a 300-meter (984-foot) lifting platform with a capacity of 67,000 metric tons, more than twice the lifting capacity of the next-largest installation, according to Saronic’s announcement Thursday.
Saronic plans to invest more than $3 billion in the project, which it says could eventually support up to 10,000 direct jobs.

According to Saronic’s Port Alpha development plans, the initial phase will accommodate ships measuring up to approximately 850 feet, with future expansion potentially supporting vessels exceeding 1,200 feet.
Saronic is also working with South Korea’s Samsung Heavy Industries as it develops its shipbuilding capabilities.

items.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
points: Minister for School Education, Tamil Development, Information and Publicity, Rajmohan, addresses the Achievers Appreciation Day at VIT Vellore on Thursday.
G.Viswanathan, founder & chancellor, VIT, is also seen. | Photo Credit: C.
VENKATACHALAPATHY Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Thursday said that the State government will not shut down even a single government school on the basis of low enrollment of students.
“New teaching methods such as teaching mathematics through stories and improvements in curriculum have been introduced to boost enrolment in government schools,” he said.
It comes in the backdrop of closure of around 94,000 government schools as against 51,000 private schools that were opened in the country in the past decade.
“In Tamil Nadu, 246 government schools had been shut during the same period.
At present, around 1,200 schools have zero enrolment,” he said.
Sankar Viswanathan and Sekar Viswanathan, vice presidents, VIT, and Premalatha, District Educational Officer (Vellore), were among others present on the occasion.

Officials said that they spotted a speeding car during a patrol led by forest range officer N.
Saravanan in the Neelakandaranpet Reserve Forest (RF).
The team tried to stop the car along with the help of police personnel, but in vain.
Forest officials and the police chased the car for around 500 metres and cornered the car at an isolated location near Sholinghur town.
The team arrested the three persons after they found red sanders in the vehicle.
The gang learnt the forests around Sholinghur town have a sizable number of red sanders that are cultivated by the Forest Department as part of an afforestation programme over a decade ago.
A case was registered and the gang members were lodged at Central Prison in Vellore.

items.title: Dhinakaran urges quality checks on Children’s Day cakes
points: Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK) general secretary T.T.V.
Dhinakaran. | Photo Credit: ASHOK R AMMK founder T.T.V.

Dhinakaran on Thursday urged the Tamil Nadu government to ensure that cakes procured for distribution to students of government and government-aided schools on Children’s Day were subjected to proper quality checks before being distributed.

Mr. Dhinakaran alleged that cakes purchased from various companies had been lying unattended in vehicles for the past four days without proper storage or preservation, raising concerns over their safety.

Pointing out that the cakes had reportedly been transported over long distances, Mr. Dhinakaran in a social media post said it was essential to verify their manufacturing and expiry dates, storage conditions and quality.
He said reports of improper storage had caused concern among parents, particularly in view of earlier complaints about the quality of food served under the school breakfast and mid-day meal schemes.
Mr. Dhinakaran urged the School Education Department to ensure that only safe and quality cakes reached children.

items.title: CMC to organise exhibition, poster competition to mark World Diabetes Day
points: The Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes & Metabolism, Christian Medical College, Vellore, will organise an awareness exhibition and poster competition on November 13 at its campus in commemoration of World Diabetes Day 2026.
As part of the awareness initiative, free blood glucose screening will be offered to all participants along with foot and eye examinations.
Awareness sessions will be conducted creatively through puppet shows, posters, and interactive games, making the learning experience engaging and memorable for people of all ages, the release said.

items.title: Exclusive | Affordablity Is Key To AI Success In India: Peak XV's Rajan Anandan
points: AI in India will be "won by Indian firms," Peak XV Managing Director Rajan Anandan has told NDTV, citing the growing volume of money that is being channelled into the sector.

In an exclusive conversation with NDTV CEO and Editor-in-Chief Rahul Kanwal in Walk the Talk, Anandan said while the initiative started late in India, as with most things, the country catches up remarkably fast.
The big impediment for developing AI in India was the lack of GPUs -- Graphic Processing Units that are like building blocks to train AI.
At the end of 2025, India had less than 10,000 active GPUs -- which is less than any top university in the US have.
Instead of the elaborate 15, 20 trillion parameter models that the US firms are building to train AGI, India is building 100 billion parameters, and they are doing it at an extremely low cost.
"In 2015, India had only one space tech startup.

Nallasivan on the basis of petitions from residents. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Encroachments, mostly houses and petty shops, were demolished on Islamiya College Road in Vaniyambadi town in Tirupattur on Thursday to provide easy access for…
Officials of State Highways, which executed the work, said that most of the 40 encroachments on the stretch were built more than a decade ago.
These structures are mostly extensions of existing shops and commercial establishments that reduced the total road space on the stretch.
“Such extensions of buildings have affected traffic movement, especially ambulances and other vehicles, on the stretch.
The drive was aimed at the safety of pedestrians, especially students, and to provide more road space for vehicles,” K.
Baburaj, Assistant Engineer (AE), State Highways (Vaniyambadi), told The Hindu.
Pedestrians, especially students, found it difficult to use the stretch due to encroachments.

items.title: Five e-scooters catch fire in Ranipet
points: Police said that an electrical short circuit could have been the reason for the incident. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT Five electric scooters caught fire at the showroom at Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town in Ranipet on Thursday.
Suresh, 49, a resident of Walajah town, was running an e-scooter showroom on Bazaar Street in Kaveripakkam village near Walajah town.
Initial inquiry revealed that, Suresh reportedly plugged in the vehicles to charge the batteries, but apparently forgot to disconnect the power supply before closing the showroom on Wednesday.
On Thursday, a few residents alerted Suresh about smoke in the showroom.
Police said that when he opened the showroom, Suresh saw that five e-scooters were gutted and 10 other vehicles were damaged in the fire.
The police said this was not the first time that electric scooters had caught fire.
In February 2023, an electric scooter parked on the veranda of a house in Vaniyambadi near Tirupattur caught fire.
The fire gutted his bike and the meter box.

items.title: SIR: Draft electoral roll released in Vellore, nearby districts
points: District Collector P.S.Leela Alex releasing the Special draft electoral rolls in the presence of all political parties in Vellore on Thursday. | Photo Credit: C.

Venkatachalapathy The draft electoral rolls for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2027 were released on Thursday for Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts, with women voters higher than men voters.
Leela Alex released the draft electoral rolls at the Collectorate in Vellore in the presence of representatives of recognised political parties and district officials.
As per the rolls, the draft tally of voters in Vellore district, which comprises five Assembly constituencies, is 11,59,481 voters (5,61,407 men; 5,97,901 women; and 173 others).

Among Assembly seats, Gudiyatham has the highest number of voters, with a total of 2,53,706 voters (1,23,258 men; 1,30,414 women; 34 others), followed by Vellore Anaicut (2,41,141 total voters) and Katpadi 2,30,996 total voters.
In Tiruvannamalai, the draft electoral rolls, which were released by DEO Vandhana Garg, have a total of 19,47,156 voters: 9,56,160 men; 9,90,840 women; and 156 others.

items.title: Gold drops to over one-year low as fading Middle East peace hopes fan inflation fears
points: Nov 12 (Reuters) - Gold prices slid 3% on Thursday, extending losses for a third straight session to hit a more-than-one-year low, as oil prices climbed on fading hopes for peace in the Middle East that spurred fears of higher inflation and elevated…
Spot gold dipped 2.7% to $3,880.93 per ounce by 1:53 p.m.
US gold futures for December delivery settled 2.9% lower at $3,885.30 per ounce.
US President Donald Trump said on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran, quashing hopes of a deal to end the conflict.

A hot US inflation reading on Tuesday, hawkish remarks from Fed officials this week and a US dollar rally to a near 19-month high "are working to press the gold market lower," said Jim Wyckoff, a market analyst at American Gold Exchange.
Traders see an 87% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move also increased.

points: The chargesheet against Veeramani and two of his drivers, submitted in the designated court for POCSO Act cases, was based on a complaint lodged by a minor girl.
According to police sources, the survivor alleged in her complaint that she was sexually exploited by Veeramani.
She had identified the octogenarian businessman during an identification process conducted by the special investigation team (SIT).
Veeramani is facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and a case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004.
The cases involve more than 10 survivors who alleged that they were sexually abused by him.

Prakash Kanniah, one of the accused wanted in connection with the cases, is believed to be in the U.K. After the police took steps to revoke his passport and obtain an arrest warrant from the designated court, which is required to issue a Red Corner…
